message.content:
In Blackjack an Ace is a “flexible” card – it can count as either **1** or **11**, whichever gives the hand the best possible total without busting.  

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **First Ace in a hand** | You may choose 1 or 11. Most players will count it as 11 unless that would cause a bust. |
| **Second Ace in a hand** | If you already have an Ace counted as 11, the second Ace is usually counted as 1 (so you don’t exceed 21). |
| **Two Aces together** | Commonly split into two separate hands (if the casino allows splitting Aces). Each new hand starts with one Ace, which can then be treated as 1 or 11 depending on the next card. |
| **Natural Blackjack** | An Ace plus any 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K) gives a “blackjack” (21) and usually pays 3:2. |
| **Bust scenario** | If counting an Ace as 11 would push the hand over 21, the Ace automatically “drops” to 1. |

So, the Ace’s value is dynamic: it’s 11 when it helps, but it can switch to 1 to avoid busting. This flexibility is what makes the Ace the most valuable card in Blackjack.
